newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up in active trade on IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up in active trade on IMF news.

text.p: Despite several bouts of profit-taking on bank and finance issues, Thai stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday as investors welcomed news that Thailand would seek help from IMF, brokers said.

"The market hadn't yet been overbought as many had thought. There was a lot of profit-taking in bank and finance issues in the afternoon but the market managed to rise. I think the market gained because of positive reaction toward Thailand's seeking IMF help," said Songyos Kulvichien of Securities One.
The composite SET index closed 1.49 points higher to 682.16 on 9.04 billion baht turnover.
Brokers said there were good signs that the market would rise further after it gained for the fourth consecutive trading day on Tuesday because of the IMF news.
Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Monday that he would meet IMF officials this week to seek advice on how to tackle the Thai economic crisis.
Brokers said the appointment of central bank deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi to succeed outgoing governor Rerngchai Marakanond would not cause any negative impact on the market.
Outgoing Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai said on Tuesday his decision to quit was prompted by recent public criticism of his performance and political pressure on him to leave office.
"I think the new governor Chaiyawat could work with IMF or World Bank officials smoothly because he knows those guys very well," said Songyos.
Brokers said foreigners were quite active on Tuesday as they bought some bank and finance stocks.
Total net buying by foreigners on Monday amounted to 328 million baht.
The SET-50 index advanced 0.16 point to 52.17.

Bangkok Bank topped the active list in terms of value, falling one baht to 179. Nava Finance advanced 0.25 to 32.25 and Eastern Water Resources Development and Management Plc, which debuted on Monday, rose 2.25 baht to 45.25 and up from its initial public offer price of 30.

Brokers said they expected the market to move in a narrow range and may fall slightly on Wednesday as investors awaited key economic indicators to be released by the central bank on Thursday. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
